featured_reviews.name: tanmay rao
featured_reviews.review_text:
Pratap Lunch Home is a great spot if you’re craving prawns or fish. I tried their butter garlic prawns (4/5), tawa surmai fry (4/5), and Chettinad prawn biryani (4/5). It’s a chill place with a coastal vibe and homely food—highly recommend for a quick lunch.
Top Dishes
•	Butter garlic prawns: Fresh and flavorful, hitting all the right garlicky notes without overpowering the seafood.
•	Tawa surmai fry: Crispy edges with balanced spices, showcasing the fish’s natural freshness.
•	Chettinad prawn biryani: Spicy, aromatic, and generously portioned for a satisfying coastal twist.
Vibe and Service
The relaxed, sea-inspired ambience pairs perfectly with the comforting, home-style cooking. Quick service makes it ideal for lunch breaks in the Fort area.

featured_reviews.name: Niki Mitra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Discover the flavors of the sea at Pratap Lunch Home, a hidden restaurant de fruits de mer in the heart of Fort, Mumbai! This seafood and non-veg lover's paradise is a must-visit for any food enthusiast.

The LOVE:

- Delicious Food: The dishes are packed with flavor, and the portions are generous.
- Friendly Staff: The team is attentive and welcoming, making sure you feel at home.
- Cozy Ambiance: The AC section is a blessing, especially during peak hours.
- Alcohol Served: With a 10% VAT, you can pair your meal with a drink of your choice.

Must-Try Dishes:

- Mutton Bhuna: Tender, spicy, and utterly addictive. The quantity is impressive, and the quality shines through.
- Prawns Chilly Roast: Fresh, flavorful, and perfectly cooked. A must-try for seafood lovers.

We were impressed by the food, service, and ambiance. While peak hours can get busy, the wait is worth it. We're already planning our next visit to try more of their menu offerings.

If you're a seafood or non-veg lover, Pratap Lunch Home is a must-visit destination. With its rich flavors and cozy atmosphere, it's a great spot for a night out with friends or a special occasion.

Lobster Chilly Roast - This was my favourite. Unbelievably good! I also liked how they were transparent in showing us the sizes and prices of the lobster they had in their catch and let us choose as per our preference. (5/5)
King Prawns Ghee Roast - Also really good. (5/5)
Shell Fish Sukka - Good masala but we were not blown away. We also had to be extra careful while eating as not all hard debris were cleaned from the shell fish. (3/5)

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Aman Bhonsle
featured_reviews.review_text: This unassuming spot might just serve some of the best fried prawns in the city. The tiny interiors and no-frills ambiance could easily mislead a first-time visitor, but the food quickly sets the record straight. The prawns are succulent and perfectly cooked, encased in a crisp, red coloured batter that achieves just the right balance of texture and flavour. The accompanying green chutney is a standout, adding a zesty punch that elevates the dish to another level. At Rs. 234 for a modest 150g portion, it’s not exactly a budget option, but the quality makes it a fair deal. These prawns would pair beautifully with a chilled beverage of your choice if you’re planning a casual meal at home. That said, there’s a certain charm in enjoying them right there, standing on the street. The service is quick, making it a convenient stop before catching a movie at the nearby Metro Theatre. Whether you’re in the mood for fried fish, chicken, prawns, or Pomfret, this spot delivers a consistently satisfying, indulgent experience—a classic that’s earned its reputation in the area.

Just experienced a fantastic meal at the iconic Bharat Excellensea, a 35-year-old gem in Mumbai's Ballard Estate! The restaurant has been recently revamped, and the ambiance is now even more inviting. But the real star is the food!

As a self-proclaimed seafood addict, I was in heaven. I sampled a wide range of dishes, each bursting with flavor and freshness.

The Tom Kha Soup was a fragrant and comforting start. The Prawns Butter Garlic were perfectly cooked and incredibly flavorful. The *Yellow Chili Prawns  packed a delicious spicy punch. The Surmai Masala Fry was a classic done exceptionally well. The Thalasseri Clams were a fiery delight, showcasing the flavors of Kerala. The Rawas Gassi was a rich and creamy Mangalorean-style curry. The Neer Dosa and Appam were the perfect accompaniments to soak up the delicious gravies.

But the real surprise was the Sitaphal Tricones Holige! This innovative dessert was a delightful fusion of Indian and modern flavors. A must-try!

Overall:
Bharat Excellensea is a must-visit for any seafood lover in Mumbai. The restaurant offers a wide variety of fresh, flavorful dishes with influences from across India's coastal regions. The recent revamp has enhanced the dining experience, making it a perfect spot for a special occasion or a memorable meal. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Debabrata Golder
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you are a seafood lover looking for an authentic and budget-friendly meal near Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CST), Sandeep Gomantak Hotel is an absolute must-visit.
Getting There & Parking
The restaurant is incredibly convenient if you are traveling by train, located just a short 5 to 7-minute walk from the CST station. I highly recommend that you go by walk only. Because it is situated in a bustling, crowded area, there is absolutely no parking available. Trying to find a spot for your vehicle nearby is a major problem and will only add unnecessary hassle to your meal, so walking is definitely the smartest option.
Ambiance & Service
Despite being a busy eatery, the management does a great job of maintaining the space. The dining area is kept very neat and clean, making for a comfortable environment to enjoy your meal. Additionally, the service is impressively fast. The staff is efficient and attentive, ensuring you get your food quickly even during peak lunch or dinner hours.
The Food
The star of the show here is undoubtedly the authentic Konkan-style cooking. The fish items are perfectly spiced, incredibly fresh, and exceptionally tasty. What makes it even better is that everything is well under budget, offering fantastic value for money without compromising on flavor. If you visit, you absolutely must try the crab—it is wonderfully prepared and easily one of the standout dishes on the menu.
Verdict
Overall, Sandeep Gomantak offers a fantastic, no-frills dining experience that hits all the right notes for coastal food cravings. Fast service, clean surroundings, and mouth-watering seafood make it a true hidden gem. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Gaurav Biswas
featured_reviews.review_text:
Waited for 15 minutes to get a place.
They serve all sorts of packet Chaknas here like Moong Dal, Chakli, Seng, Chana, Roasted Chana Etc. These are all reasonably priced between 20 to 40.

We order Bombil Fry, Chicken Sukka, Kori Rotti and Neer Dosa & Solkadi
Being married to a Mangalorean and been a regular to Mangalorean outlets back in Kudla I know the taste very well. This was nowhere near sadly. The Bombil Fry being a Maharashtrian special was just oil fried with light red batter rather than Rawa Fry. Killed the appetite completely unfortunately. It was served a small bowl of Coconut gravy which was again very bland.

The Chicken Sukka was too bland. Quantity was ample but the taste was honestly bland. I tried to finish it with the Neer Dosa since Bhakri wasn't available.

Neer Dosa again was served with a small bowl of Coconut gravy as usual bland.

The Kori Rotti being a staple food amongst mangaloreans was a major let down. It didn't have any flavor and even had sasive(Mustard) in it which was unlike of any Mangalorean Outlet. My wife finished it with a lot of difficulty.

The only savior was the Solkadi and it was really tasty and thick. It was too good and cheap at the same time.

Overall verdict is it's a cheap and pocket friendly place. The food was 2/5. Drinks are probably cheap since everyone was busy consuming that. Solkadi 6/5. The staff were always on the feet and ready to attend.

Visited Mahesh Lunch Home and had a wonderful dining experience. We tried the Butter Garlic Prawns, Crab Lollipop, Jumbo Tawa Prawns, and Chicken Biryani. The seafood was fresh, perfectly cooked, and packed with flavor. The Butter Garlic Prawns were rich and delicious, while the Jumbo Tawa Prawns stood out with their excellent seasoning. The Crab Lollipop was crispy and enjoyable, and the Chicken Biryani was aromatic and satisfying.

A special mention for their Solkadi, which is always on the darker side. While it has a distinctive flavor, I feel a slightly lighter preparation could bring more subtlety and balance, making it even more refreshing and enjoyable to sip alongside the seafood.

The service was attentive, and the overall ambiance made for a great meal. Definitely a place worth visiting for seafood lovers. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a very satisfying dining experience here. The Surumai tawa fish fry was excellent—perfectly cooked with a great balance of spices that enhanced the flavour of the fish without being too heavy. The Chicken Chettinad was amazing—rich, aromatic, and authentic, with a well-rounded masala that really stood out. The squid was also quite tasty, fresh, and cooked just right.

The place itself has a nice ambience, is clean and hygienic, and the overall quality of food is clearly well maintained. The staff are very friendly, polite, and attentive, which adds positively to the experience.

While the prices are on the higher side, the quality, hygiene, and taste justify the cost. A good place for quality food and a relaxed dining experience—definitely worth a visit. Only issue is Parking. Better to go in a taxi.

The vibe of the place is great, making it a perfect spot for lunch with a comfortable and lively atmosphere.

featured_reviews.name: Daddyslittlelunchbox
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mahesh Lunch Lounge was an absolute standout and easily one of our best meals in India. We chose to eat here over the Taj after it was strongly recommended by locals — and we are so glad we listened. From start to finish, the experience was fantastic.

The food was exceptional, especially the seafood. The tiger prawns were MASSIVE — genuinely some of the biggest prawns we’ve ever seen, let alone eaten. They were cooked perfectly, full of flavour, and without doubt the best prawns we had in India. That’s saying something, especially as we truly believed Kerala couldn’t be beaten when it came to seafood.

Service was attentive and efficient without being overbearing, and the prices were surprisingly good for the quality and portion sizes. One bit of advice: order your starters before committing to mains — the portions are generous and we definitely over-ordered because everything sounded too good to miss (no regrets, just very full 😅).

Overall, Mahesh Lunch Lounge completely lived up to the hype and then some. Incredible food, huge portions, great service, and excellent value. If you’re debating where to eat — go here.

Visited this restaurant on the way to Crawford Market. I’ve been coming here since childhood—not very regularly, but occasionally.I went for kheema pav, but the owner suggested bheja along with kheema pav, so I went with his recommendation.

When the dish arrived, the portion size was quite small and didn’t feel worth ₹240. On top of that, they charge ₹20 extra for pav, which feels a bit excessive. The taste was very good—rich and flavorful—but slightly too spicy and oily for my liking.

In the afternoon, the place is usually packed, especially for non-vegetarian dishes. However, as a local Mumbaikar, I do feel the pricing is on the higher side. Either the cost should be more reasonable or the portion size should be increased to justify it.

The owner was actively moving around, asking customers for feedback and promoting items like fish fry, caramel custard, and solkadhi. While this does help in building customer relationships, a major drawback comes at the time of billing—they do not accept UPI payments, only cash.

We left full and sent them a lot of blessings for such delicious food!  We were hungry so didn't have the patience to take pictures to post.
The Fried Bombil, Crab Lollipop, Prawns Masala, and Prawns Pulav were outstanding. The river prawns were sweet and cooked perfectly.Mutton Khima was flavourful, well-spiced, and delicious. Their last portion of caramel custard had our name on it, so glad! That was so good too.
The staff is incredibly polite and attentive. A special thanks to the manager, Shridhar, who suggested a few items every single recommendation was spot on and scrumptious.
The restaurant is located in a crowded area and the street is not well lit but the food is so good that the surroundings do not matter. It is a definitive must-try place if you are in the area. We only wish they had a branch in Pune!

featured_reviews.name: Cyrus Doodhmal
featured_reviews.review_text:
For our 32nd anniversary, my wife and I wanted to mark the occasion somewhere special, and we couldn’t have chosen better than Oriental Blossom at Hotel Marine Plaza, perfectly located along the beautiful stretch of Marine Drive.

The Oriental Blossom has a quiet, understated elegance—no frills or over-the-top decor, just a warm, inviting space with soft lighting and tasteful wooden accents that create a cozy, intimate vibe. The moment we walked in, we were greeted with a warm smile by Isha, the gracious hostess, who made us feel instantly at ease.

The menu is a delightful mix of Cantonese and Szechuan dishes, thoughtfully curated by Chef Huang Te Sing, who clearly knows how to bring out authentic flavors while keeping things simple, fresh, and satisfying.

We kicked off our meal with a comforting bowl of Seafood Coriander Soup for me and Sweetcorn Crab Soup for my better half. Both were flavorful, hearty, and just the right way to start. The wontons and crispy calamari followed, and I have to say—they stole the show for me. The wontons were delicate yet packed with flavor, and the calamari was perfectly crisp, with just the right amount of seasoning to keep us reaching for more.

For the mains, we couldn’t resist the barbecue pork and stir-fried duck. Both were cooked to perfection—tender, juicy, and bursting with bold, savory flavors. We paired them with egg fried rice and Hakka noodles, which balanced the richness of the meats beautifully, making for a satisfying and comforting meal.

What truly stood out, though, was the impeccable service. Maitre D’ Able Pathan and Hostess Isha were attentive without being overbearing, offering thoughtful recommendations and ensuring that everything was just right. Their warmth and professionalism added a personal touch that made our afternoon feel even more special.

The combination of delicious food, warm service, and the serene ambiance made our anniversary lunch one we’ll always cherish.

In a city overflowing with dining options, The Oriental Blossom stands out—not just for its food, but for the way it makes you feel. It’s not just a restaurant; it’s a place where special memories are made.

A heartfelt thank you to Chef Huang Te Sing, Able Pathan, and Isha for making our celebration so memorable.

-b. Pomfret: 9/10
-c. Bombil: 7/10

The rice bhakari tasted awesome when it was hot.
Dry Prawns/Jhinga/Javla tasted good with the bhakari.
The pomfret fish and curry was very fresh and tasty.
Solkadhi was chilled, felt refreshing and tasted good.

Gulab Jamun was the worst. Hard, dry and low on flavor.

Restaurant is smaller compared to the one near kemps corner. Cleanliness was decent. No washrooms. Only a basin is available. No Queue when we arrived at 8pm. But a queue started building later on.

Group of 4. Saturday Dinner. Mid April 2026.

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Aman Bhonsle
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’ve been coming here since I was a kid—long enough that I’m pretty sure my first real chicken tandoori happened right here. The menu has changed over the years, sure, but the place has stubbornly refused to lose its old-school charm. Portions? Still generous. This isn’t food that apologizes for itself.

The Chinese starters have absolutely nothing to do with China—and thank God for that. They’re loud, greasy, Indo-Chinese comfort bombs that slap hard. Pick any of the chicken gravies and you’re in a good place emotionally. I will say this: the kebabs feel a little smaller than they used to. Shrinkflation? Age? Betrayal? I don’t know. Still good. Just… noted.

Twenty-one years ago, when I was a broke college student and my parents would leave town—trusting me alone at home far more than they should have—I ordered from here like it was a civic duty. My friends from that era still remember how much food I could put away from this place. This is not health food. No one here is pretending otherwise. But it hits all the right buttons.

I ordered so often that before food apps, before algorithms, the guy answering the phone knew my order just by hearing my voice. Within an hour, like clockwork, the food would land at my parents’ place. I’d sit there demolishing it while binge-watching American TV, living my best irresponsible life.

Some of my old favorites are gone now, but the current menu holds its own. I’ve eaten here with my wife, with her family, across decades and phases of life. Parking is usually manageable. There’s a mosque nearby, Bombay Hospital around the corner, and the now-shuttered Liberty Cinema—where I watched half my childhood movies. The area isn’t glamorous. It doesn’t try to be. It’s old Mumbai, still breathing, still feeding people properly.

This place survives because it’s trusted. Because it’s consistent. Because people who know food still show up here quietly and eat without drama.

What’s instantly noticeable is who eats here.
Old-school locals, serious food people, and a steady stream of expats—especially Arab expats—who clearly didn’t wander in by accident.

Late at night, you’ll see many happy Muslim families settling in comfortably, sharing plates, unhurried, treating the place like an extension of home.

Go without hesitation.
Ask the manager what to order.

Then sit down and let them take care of you.

Visited Malvani Klub Restaurant at Lalbaugh with my wife, and we were genuinely impressed with the food, service, and overall experience. We ordered the Bangda Thali and Prawns Thali, and both were absolutely delicious. The Prawns Fry served as a starter was perfectly spiced and crispy, while the Solkadi was refreshing and authentic.

The Bangda fry in the thali had that perfect Malvani masala flavour, and the curries were rich, aromatic, and truly reminded us of homely Maharashtrian coastal food. The prawns curry was equally flavourful, and the chapatis were soft and fresh.

Apart from the excellent food, the staff deserves a special mention — very polite, friendly, and attentive. They made the dining experience even better with their warm hospitality.

If you love Maharashtrian or Malvani cuisine, this place is a must-visit. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Nitant Pandhare
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Coastal Paradise for Seafood Lovers! 🦀✨
Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

If you are looking for authentic Malvani flavors in Mumbai, Malvani Klub is an absolute gem. We visited recently and were blown away by the freshness of the seafood and the richness of their traditional masalas.

The Highlights:

Starters: We started with the Fried Bombil and Prawns Fry. The Bombil (Bombay Duck) was perfectly crisp on the outside and buttery-soft inside—just the way it should be! The prawns were succulent, fresh, and seasoned to perfection.

The Thali Experience:

Surmai Thali: The fish was a generous size, well-marinated, and paired beautifully with the authentic Malvani rassa.

Chicken Komdi Vade Thali: The vade were fluffy and hot, making them the perfect companion to the spicy, flavorful chicken curry.

Crab Thali: A true standout! The crab was meaty and the gravy had that deep, soulful coastal spice kick.

Kolambi Bhaat: This was a revelation! Fragrant rice cooked with juicy prawns and a blend of aromatic spices. It’s a must-order if you want a hearty, one-pot Malvani meal.

Solkadhi: No Malvani meal is complete without this. Their Solkadhi was refreshing, creamy, and had the perfect balance of kokum and garlic to cleanse the palate.

The food here is amazingly awesome and truly authentic. The portions are satisfying, and the taste reminds you of a home-cooked meal in the Konkan belt. Whether you're a hardcore seafood fan or a chicken lover, this place will not disappoint!

Recommendation: Go hungry, and definitely don't miss the Kolambi Bhaat!

Had an amazing experience at this Malvani restaurant! The food truly felt like a comforting home-cooked meal, full of authentic coastal flavors and made with so much care.
We tried the crab lollipop, surmai thali, bombil thali, mutton thali and dal rice—every single dish was absolutely delicious. The seafood was fresh and perfectly cooked, especially the surmai and bombil, which had that authentic homemade taste. The mutton thali was rich, flavorful, and incredibly satisfying, while the dal rice added a simple, comforting touch to the entire meal.
What really stood out was the homely vibe—not just in the food but also in the warm and welcoming service. It honestly felt like eating at someone’s home rather than a restaurant.
Highly recommend this place if you’re looking for genuine, soulful Malvani food. Will definitely be coming back again!!!
